Pocket Reader

ESP32-C3 based, pocket-size, open-source e-paper book reader. The model below is generated from real placement data — the position, size and height of every part are read from the hardware/pcb/placement.csv file.

Thickness budget

The 13 mm body was not an arbitrary choice — it follows from the sum of the layers below. If you change the panel or the battery, this table must be recalculated.

#LayerThicknessNote
1Front bezel (over the glass edge)1.20 mmThe case's panel frame
2E-paper glass1.05 mm59.2 × 29.2 mm
3FPC fold clearance0.80 mmAbove the tallest part
4PCB1.60 mm45 × 24 mm, 2 layers
5Tallest part (ESP32 module)2.50 mmButtons 3.5 mm — in the case cutout
6Li-Po cell4.00 mm26 × 21 × 4.5 mm pocket
7Back cover1.60 mm4 × M1.6 screws
Total12.75 mm0.25 mm margin → body 13.0 mm
Correction. The first design had a 58 × 30 mm body. But the panel glass is 59.2 × 29.2 mm — it would never fit into a 58 mm case. The body was corrected to 62 × 32 mm: 62 − 59.2 = 2.8 mm, i.e. a 1.4 mm bezel margin on each side of the glass. This dimension is derived from the glass size in case.scad, not chosen freely.

PCB layout

The technical drawings below are generated from the hardware/pcb/placement.csv file. Each part's pad, silkscreen and courtyard are drawn at true size.

This is a placement proposal, not a production-ready PCB. Traces are not routed; thermal and EMC optimisation has not been done. The real layout must be done in KiCad and pass DRC. The repository deliberately ships no Gerbers: 13 pin numbers are still awaiting verification from the datasheet.

Drawings generated from data

The 3D model on this page and the 2D technical drawings beside it read the same placement file. Two hand-maintained coordinate lists in separate places would inevitably drift apart; using a single source prevents that structurally.

placement.csv → 64 parts connections.csv → 170 connections gen_placement.py --check → no overlaps gen_pcb_layout.py → 3 SVGs pocket-reader.net → KiCad case.scad → STL
Verification. gen_placement.py --check checks that every part stays inside the board, that no two overlap, and that the placement holds exactly the same set of parts as gen_netlist.py. 64 parts, 0 overlaps.
